source.title: FAM: Relative Flatness Aware Minimization
source.authors: Linara Adilova; A. Abourayya; Jian-Ning Li; Amin Dada; Henning Petzka; Jan Egger; J. Kleesiek; Michael Kamp

record.tranche_reason: Uses relative flatness as a regularizer intended to improve generalization and reports how FAM performs. It does not test the claim versions’ specific interventions or measurements.
record.gate_note: FAM, baseline, and SAM performance results are included under fits_no_version: they test relative-flatness regularization against image-classification accuracy, skull reconstruction metrics, and RTE validation accuracy, none of which matches a listed version’s specific test. Cited results from other studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses a relative-flatness measure to construct FAM and evaluates its performance against baseline training and SAM. It does not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, correlate that measure with generalization gaps, or compare its ranking with alternative measures. Its other experiments do not test V1–V6 or V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that FAM improves generalization across several applications and architectures, outperforming baseline training and sometimes SAM. They qualify the theoretical connection by locally constant labels, leave layer-choice comparisons for future work, and warn that excessive regularization produces unvaried skull reconstructions.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a relative-flatness regularizer to training and compares with baseline and SAM; does not test the claim versions’ specified recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Regularization coefficient λ affects results; the authors state that over-regularization can lead to unvaried skull reconstructions. The choice of layer is not systematically compared; comprehensive study is left for future work.

fits_no_version.finding: FAM has the highest reported image-classification accuracy on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100; SAM has the highest on SVHN and FashionMNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative-flatness regularization can improve image-classification accuracy in some model and dataset settings.

fits_no_version.finding: FAM improves epoch-200 DSC on both skull evaluation sets despite higher training loss. At λ = 0.1 and 0.7, high DSC accompanies unvaried reconstructions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative-flatness regularization can improve skull reconstruction metrics, but excessive regularization can undermine case-specific reconstruction.

fits_no_version.finding: Across five BERT fine-tuning runs, FAM increases mean RTE validation accuracy from 0.67364 to 0.6982; validation-loss growth persists but is less pronounced.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: FAM can improve RTE fine-tuning validation performance in this setup.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says code is available at github but provides no URL
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2nd Annual Workshop on Topology, Algebra, and Geometry in Machine Learning (TAG-ML) at ICML 2023
record.problems: Image-classification baseline and SAM numbers are lower than those reported in the original SAM paper, and the authors attribute this to implementation differences. The SVHN setup uses only the main training dataset rather than extra data. Training-to-test gaps are not reported for image classification or RTE. The layer choice is not comprehensively studied. Skull results include two evaluation sets of 100 images each, and the authors caution that over-regularization can produce unvaried reconstructions.
record.rows_left_out: For skull reconstruction, omitted the separately reported HD, HD95, and epoch-100 DSC/HD/HD95 values in Table 2 to stay within the 60-row limit while retaining baseline and all λ conditions for the primary DSC metric on both evaluation sets. Also omitted other text-described curves and boxplot distributions because they provide no additional extractable numeric values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label held-out generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under specified tuning budgets, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal alongside weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted table values match the supplied text. These are method-performance rows and belong under fits_no_version rather than claim-verdict evidence. Section 4.1.2 says Adam performed best against SGD and rmsprop during optimizer selection, but supplies neither comparative results nor enough tuning detail to test V4. The locally constant-label qualification concerns the cited relative-flatness theory; it does not establish a failure of V7's specified empirical correlation.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as network width passes the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under limited and broader tuning, including weight-decay and optimizer-switch comparisons.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout’s effects across training-set sizes and its removal alongside weight decay.
The specified magnitude-scaled perturbation measure and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

relation.reason: Flatness-related generalization findings motivate FAM; the study evaluates FAM against baseline training and SAM without testing a listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study uses relative flatness to construct a regularizer and reports method performance. It does not test V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap correlation, or ranking against alternative measures; its other experiments do not test V1–V8.

source_check.notes: Table 2's DSC columns are recoverable from the supplied text; unmarked columns report epoch 200. Table 1 supports the recorded CIFAR100 values despite different figures in Section 4.1.2; high skull DSC at λ=0.1 or 0.7 accompanies unvaried reconstructions.
